Homework exercise · Week 6

Remix Studio

Scratch (offline app) Work in pairs

Goal: practice "blocks to words" for next week's Python, and level up one of your own Scratch projects. Time: about 10 minutes for Core. Tool: paper + Scratch app (offline).

Build steps

Part 1 (paper, 4 minutes): on your homework sheet, write the Python line for each block. Use your card sort as a dictionary:

  • move 50 steps
  • turn left 90 degrees
  • say "Hi!"
  • repeat 3
  • set lives to 3

Part 2 (Scratch, 6 minutes):

  1. Open one of your projects from weeks 1-5 (File > Load from your computer).
  2. Add one improvement: a sound effect, a new backdrop, a score or lives variable, a key that does something, a My Block, or a message between two sprites.
  3. Test it with the green flag.
  4. Save it with a new name ending in -v2 (for example apple-catch-v2). Your old version stays safe.

The script in words (one example improvement)

Adding a "you win" message to Apple Catch, on the Apple, at the bottom of the forever loop:

  • if score = 10 then
    • say "You win!" for 2 seconds
    • stop all

Expected behavior

Your -v2 project still does everything the old one did, plus your one new improvement, every time you click the green flag.

Checklist

Stuck? Open a hint

Try on your own first. Hints open one at a time, from a small nudge to a bigger one. None of them gives the answer away.

Hint 1: Where to look

Part 1 is like translating between two languages. Use your card sort as a dictionary and match each block to its Python line. Look at the Python names you learned for moving, turning, and printing.

Hint 2: Try this

Each block is one Python line. Numbers and words go inside the brackets. A variable block like set lives to 3 is written with an equals sign. For Part 2, pick just one small improvement and test it.

Hint 3: Almost there

Use these shapes: t.forward(____), t.left(____), print(____), and lives = ____. For repeat 3, use a line that begins for ____ in range(____):. Remember that Python needs quotes around words. For Part 2, save a new copy ending in -v2.

Back to week 6

Parents: the course folder has an automatic self-check script for the Python exercises. It is not on this website because it relies on test files that give away the answers.
